changes.resolution: Read lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex's evaluate_access/2 in full this session. Its :AllowWithRowFilter branch is `if endpoint == :TasksList and is_task_worker_only?(ctx.roles)` -- gated on :TasksList only. Every other endpoint that passes the permission check, including :TasksComplete (the policy key POST /tasks/:id/complete maps to, per endpoint_policy_key/2's clause `def endpoint_policy_key("POST", "/tasks/:id/complete"), do: :TasksComplete`), falls through to `%AccessDecision{kind: :Allow, task_scope: :all}` unconditionally -- no row filter, no assignee check. Combined with the design's already-confirmed fact that Engine.complete_task/3 has no assignee precondition, this settles: claim is NOT required before complete. §3.2's step table now authors each business step (ops-approve, ceo-co-sign) as exactly one POST .../complete call, 3 business-level dispatches total, not 5.

changes.location: §3.2 (new paragraph before the step table) and the step table itself
changes.resolution: Read lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex's handle_list/3 in full this session. Its `with` clause contains `{:ok, instance_id} <- parse_instance_id_param(Map.get(query, "instance_id"))`, passed straight into Tasks.list_tasks/2's filter map alongside a `status` param handled the same way. Settled: GET /api/v1/tasks?instance_id=<uuid>&status=PENDING is the real, shipped lookup mechanism. The step table now specifies this exact call as steps 2a/3a (produces: "ops_task"/"ceo_task"), with 2b/3b as the POST .../complete calls consuming `{{produces.ops_task.id}}`/`{{produces.ceo_task.id}}`.

Read lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex's resolve_assignee/1 in full this session: `def resolve_assignee(%Graph.Node{attributes: attributes}) do {Map.get(attributes, "assignee_type"), Map.get(attributes, "role")} end`. For a role:-attributed HUMAN_TASK node, assignee_ref is node.attributes["role"] verbatim (e.g. "role-ops-manager", "role-ceo" from process_route_approval.yaml's node attributes). Settled: each scenario actor's create_token/3 call needs the process node's exact role string in its roles: list -- the ops-approve actor's token carries roles: ["role-ops-manager"], the CEO-co-sign actor's token carries roles: ["role-ceo"]. Stated explicitly in the step table's actor column.
